The [causes of World War II](/wiki/Causes_of_World_War_II "Causes of World War II") included unresolved tensions in the [aftermath of World War I](/wiki/Aftermath_of_World_War_I "Aftermath of World War I") and the rise of [fascism in Europe](/wiki/Fascism_in_Europe "Fascism in Europe") and [militarism in Japan](/wiki/Japanese_militarism "Japanese militarism"). Key events preceding the war included [Japan's invasion of Manchuria](/wiki/Japanese_invasion_of_Manchuria "Japanese invasion of Manchuria") in 1931, the [Spanish Civil War](/wiki/Spanish_Civil_War "Spanish Civil War"), the outbreak of the [Second Sino-Japanese War](/wiki/Second_Sino-Japanese_War "Second Sino-Japanese War") in 1937, and Germany's [annexations of Austria](/wiki/Anschluss "Anschluss") and [the Sudetenland](/wiki/Munich_Agreement "Munich Agreement"). World War II is generally considered to have begun on 1 September 1939, when [Nazi Germany](/wiki/Nazi_Germany "Nazi Germany"), under [Adolf Hitler](/wiki/Adolf_Hitler "Adolf Hitler"), [invaded Poland](/wiki/Invasion_of_Poland "Invasion of Poland"), after which the [United Kingdom](/wiki/United_Kingdom_declaration_of_war_on_Germany_(1939) "United Kingdom declaration of war on Germany (1939)") and [France declared war](/wiki/French_declaration_of_war_on_Germany_(1939) "French declaration of war on Germany (1939)") on Germany. Poland was also invaded by the [Soviet Union](/wiki/Soviet_Union "Soviet Union") in mid-September and was partitioned between Germany and the Soviet Union under the [Molotov–Ribbentrop Pact](/wiki/Molotov%E2%80%93Ribbentrop_Pact "Molotov–Ribbentrop Pact"). Sichuan :: History :: Qing dynasty :: chunk_0012
See also: [Hakka people § Sichuan](/wiki/Hakka_people#Sichuan "Hakka people")

Sichuan was originally the origin of the Deng lineage until one of them was hired as an official in Guangdong during the Ming dynasty but during the Qing plan to increase the population in 1671 they came to Sichuan again. In 1904 [Deng Xiaoping](/wiki/Deng_Xiaoping "Deng Xiaoping") was born in Sichuan.[[49]](#cite_note-Dai2009_2-50)

During the [Qing dynasty](/wiki/Qing_dynasty "Qing dynasty"), Sichuan was merged with [Shaanxi](/wiki/Shaanxi "Shaanxi") and [Shanxi](/wiki/Shanxi "Shanxi") to create "Shenzhuan" during 1680–1731 and 1735–1748.[[31]](#cite_note-Tara-32) The current borders of Sichuan (which then included [Chongqing](/wiki/Chongqing "Chongqing")) were established in the early 18th century. In the aftermath of the [Sino-Nepalese War](/wiki/Sino-Nepalese_War "Sino-Nepalese War") on China's southwestern border, the Qing gave Sichuan's provincial government direct control over the minority-inhabited areas of Sichuan west of [Kangding](/wiki/Kangding "Kangding"), which had previously been handled by an [amban](/wiki/Amban "Amban").[[47]](#cite_note-Dai-48)

A [landslide dam](/wiki/Landslide_dam "Landslide dam") on the [Dadu River](/wiki/Dadu_River_(Sichuan) "Dadu River (Sichuan)") caused by an earthquake gave way on 10 June 1786. The resulting flood killed 100,000 people.[[50]](#cite_note-51)

On December 16, 2009, the Phillies acquired starting pitcher [Roy Halladay](/wiki/Roy_Halladay "Roy Halladay") from the Toronto Blue Jays for three minor-league prospects,[[48]](#cite_note-MLB3-48) and traded Cliff Lee to the [Seattle Mariners](/wiki/Seattle_Mariners "Seattle Mariners") for three prospects.[[49]](#cite_note-MLB2-49)

On May 29, 2010, Halladay pitched a perfect game against the [Florida Marlins](/wiki/Florida_Marlins "Florida Marlins").[[d]](#endnote_NL2perfectb) In June 2010, the team's scheduled series against the Toronto Blue Jays at [Rogers Centre](/wiki/Rogers_Centre "Rogers Centre") was moved to Philadelphia, because of security concerns for the [G-20 Summit](/wiki/2010_G-20_Toronto_summit "2010 G-20 Toronto summit"). The Blue Jays wore their home white uniforms and batted last as the home team, and the [designated hitter](/wiki/Designated_hitter "Designated hitter") was used.[[50]](#cite_note-50) The game was the first occasion of the use of a designated hitter in a National League ballpark in a regular-season game; Ryan Howard was the first player to fill the role.[[51]](#cite_note-51)

Main article: [Wildlife of Mongolia](/wiki/Wildlife_of_Mongolia "Wildlife of Mongolia")

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a3/KhongorynElsCamels.jpg/250px-KhongorynElsCamels.jpg)](/wiki/File:KhongorynElsCamels.jpg)

[Bactrian camels](/wiki/Bactrian_camels "Bactrian camels") by sand dunes in Gobi Desert

The name "Gobi" is a Mongol term for a desert steppe, which usually refers to a category of arid rangeland with insufficient vegetation to support [marmots](/wiki/Marmot "Marmot") but with enough to support camels.[[62]](#cite_note-:0-65) Mongols distinguish Gobi from desert proper, although the distinction is not always apparent to outsiders unfamiliar with the Mongolian landscape.[[62]](#cite_note-:0-65)

Gobi rangelands are fragile and easily destroyed by overgrazing, which results in expansion of the true desert, a stony waste where not even [Bactrian camels](/wiki/Bactrian_camel "Bactrian camel") can survive.[[62]](#cite_note-:0-65) The arid conditions in the Gobi are attributed to the [rain shadow effect](/wiki/Rain_shadow_effect "Rain shadow effect") caused by the Himalayas. Before the Himalayas were formed by the collision of the Indo-Australian plate with the Eurasian plate 10 million years ago, Mongolia was a flourishing habitat for major fauna but still somewhat arid and cold due to distance from sources of evaporation. Sea turtle and mollusk fossils have been found in the Gobi, apart from well-known dinosaur fossils. [Tadpole shrimps](/wiki/Tadpole_shrimps "Tadpole shrimps") are still found in the Gobi today. The eastern part of Mongolia including the [Onon](/wiki/Onon_River "Onon River") and [Kherlen](/wiki/Kherlen_River "Kherlen River") rivers and [Lake Buir](/wiki/Lake_Buir "Lake Buir") form part of the [Amur river](/wiki/Amur_river "Amur river") basin draining to the Pacific Ocean. fanoutqa_032624.x:
Telephone numbers in Pakistan :: Mobile telephone numbers :: chunk_0002
Mobile telephone numbers in Pakistan are of the following format: 03XZ-YYYYYYY where X is the single letter code assigned to a specific mobile telephone operator and Z-YYYYYYY is the local telephone number from any mobile phone or landline.

* 3 - is the Mobile Access code
* Z can be any value between 0 and 9, assigned by the operator itself, except in case of SCOM where Z=5 only
* X=0 [Jazz](/wiki/Jazz_(mobile_network_operator) "Jazz (mobile network operator)")

* X=1 [Zong](/wiki/Zong_(mobile_network) "Zong (mobile network)")
* X=2 [Jazz](/wiki/Jazz_(mobile_network_operator) "Jazz (mobile network operator)")
* X=3 [Ufone](/wiki/Ufone "Ufone")
* X=4 [Telenor Pakistan](/wiki/Telenor_Pakistan "Telenor Pakistan")
* X=5 [SCO](/wiki/Special_Communications_Organization "Special Communications Organization") (Z = 5 only)
* X=7 [Zong](/wiki/Zong_(mobile_network) "Zong (mobile network)") (Z = 0 and 1 only)

Existing Codes

* 300, 301, 302, 303, 304, 305, 306, 307, 308, 309 - [Jazz](/wiki/Jazz_(mobile_network_operator) "Jazz (mobile network operator)")
* 310, 311, 312, 313, 314, 315, 316, 317, 318, 319 - [Zong](/wiki/Zong_(mobile_network) "Zong (mobile network)")
* 320, 321, 322, 323, 324, 325, 326, 327, 328, 329 - [Jazz](/wiki/Jazz_(mobile_network_operator) "Jazz (mobile network operator)")
* 330, 331, 332, 333, 334, 335, 336, 337, 338, 339 - [Ufone](/wiki/Ufone "Ufone")
* 340, 341, 342, 343, 344, 345, 346, 347, 348, 349 - [Telenor Pakistan](/wiki/Telenor_Pakistan "Telenor Pakistan")
* 370, 371 - [Zong](/wiki/Zong_(mobile_network) "Zong (mobile network)")

**Macau**[[e]](#cite_note-16) or **Macao**[[f]](#cite_note-17) is a [special administrative region](/wiki/Special_administrative_regions_of_China "Special administrative regions of China") of [China](/wiki/China "China"). It consists of the [Macau Peninsula](/wiki/Macau_Peninsula "Macau Peninsula"), the islands of [Taipa](/wiki/Taipa "Taipa") and [Coloane](/wiki/Coloane "Coloane"), the [Cotai reclamation zone](/wiki/Cotai "Cotai") between Taipa and Coloane, and several smaller islets. It borders [Zhuhai](/wiki/Zhuhai "Zhuhai") to the north and west, and it lies west of [Hong Kong](/wiki/Hong_Kong "Hong Kong"), separated by the [Pearl River estuary](/wiki/Pearl_River_estuary "Pearl River estuary"). With a population of about 720,000 people[[12]](#cite_note-18) and a land area of 32.9 square kilometres (12.7 sq mi), it is the most [densely populated region](/wiki/List_of_countries_and_dependencies_by_population_density "List of countries and dependencies by population density") in the world.

Formerly a [Portuguese](/wiki/Portuguese_Empire "Portuguese Empire") colony, the territory of [Portuguese Macau](/wiki/Portuguese_Macau "Portuguese Macau") was first leased to [Portugal](/wiki/Portugal "Portugal") by the [Ming dynasty](/wiki/Ming_dynasty "Ming dynasty") as a [trading post](/wiki/Trading_post "Trading post") in 1557. Shortly thereafter, the conclusion of the [Peace of Westphalia](/wiki/Peace_of_Westphalia "Peace of Westphalia") allowed Condé's army to return to aid Louis and his court. Condé's family was close to Anne at that time, and he agreed to help her attempt to restore the king's authority.[[23]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEPetitfils200284–87-25) The queen's army, headed by Condé, attacked the rebels in Paris; the rebels were under the political control of Anne's old friend [Marie de Rohan](/wiki/Marie_de_Rohan "Marie de Rohan"). Beaufort, who had escaped from the prison where Anne had incarcerated him five years before, was the military leader in Paris, under the nominal control of Conti. After a few battles, a political compromise was reached; the [Peace of Rueil](/wiki/Peace_of_Rueil "Peace of Rueil") was signed, and the court returned to Paris.

Unfortunately for Anne, her partial victory depended on Condé, who wanted to control the queen and destroy Mazarin's influence. It was Condé's sister who pushed him to turn against the queen. After striking a deal with her old friend Marie de Rohan, who was able to impose the nomination of [Charles de l'Aubespine, marquess of Châteauneuf](/wiki/Charles_de_L%27Aubespine "Charles de L'Aubespine") as minister of justice, Anne arrested Condé, his brother [Armand de Bourbon, Prince of Conti](/wiki/Armand_de_Bourbon,_Prince_of_Conti "Armand de Bourbon, Prince of Conti"), and the husband of their sister Anne Genevieve de Bourbon, [duchess of Longueville](/wiki/Duchess_of_Longueville "Duchess of Longueville"). This situation did not last long, and Mazarin's unpopularity led to the creation of a coalition headed mainly by Marie de Rohan and the duchess of Longueville. This aristocratic coalition was strong enough to liberate the princes, exile Mazarin, and impose a condition of virtual house arrest on Queen Anne.

For a current weather forecast, see [§ External links](#External_links).

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/8f/Acadia_National_Park%2C_frozen_lake_and_snow_covered_trees.jpg/250px-Acadia_National_Park%2C_frozen_lake_and_snow_covered_trees.jpg)](/wiki/File:Acadia_National_Park,_frozen_lake_and_snow_covered_trees.jpg)

Frozen lake and snowy trees

The region is characterized by a large seasonal variation in temperature with warm to hot summers that are often humid, and cold to severely cold winters. According to the [Köppen climate classification](/wiki/K%C3%B6ppen_climate_classification "Köppen climate classification") system, Mount Desert Island has a warm-summer [humid continental climate](/wiki/Humid_continental_climate "Humid continental climate") (*Dfb*). The average annual temperature in the park is 47.3 °F (8.5 °C). July is the warmest month with an average of 69.7 °F (20.9 °C), while January is the coldest month with an average of 23.8 °F (−4.6 °C). The record high and low temperatures are 96 °F (36 °C) and −21 °F (−29 °C), respectively. The plant [hardiness zone](/wiki/Hardiness_zone "Hardiness zone") is 5b with an average annual extreme minimum air temperature of −11.4 °F (−24.1 °C).[[49]](#cite_note-USDA-50)

Average annual precipitation in Bar Harbor is 55.54" (1411 mm). November is the wettest month with 5.89" (150 mm) of precipitation on average, while July is the driest month with 3.27" (83 mm). Precipitation days are spread evenly throughout the year with December averaging the most days with about 14, while August averages the least with about 9. The annual average days with precipitation is 139. Snow has been recorded from October to May, although the majority falls from December to March. The snowiest month is January with 18.3" (46 cm), and the annual average is 66.1" (167 cm).

In 1910, [Harry Burns Hutchins](/wiki/Harry_Burns_Hutchins "Harry Burns Hutchins") assumed the presidency, becoming the first alumnus to hold that position.[[82]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEShaw194276–80-86) He had spent seven years in [Ithaca, New York](/wiki/Ithaca,_New_York "Ithaca, New York"), where he was called by [Andrew Dickson White](/wiki/Andrew_Dickson_White "Andrew Dickson White") and [Charles Kendall Adams](/wiki/Charles_Kendall_Adams "Charles Kendall Adams") to establish the [Cornell Law School](/wiki/Cornell_Law_School "Cornell Law School").[[82]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEShaw194276–80-86) Hutchins then became the dean of the law school at his alma mater, where he introduced the [case method](/wiki/Case_method "Case method") of instruction.[[82]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEShaw194276–80-86) Hutchins was acting president when Angell was absent.[[82]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEShaw194276–80-86) During his presidency, Hutchins established the [Graduate School](/wiki/Rackham_Graduate_School "Rackham Graduate School"),[[82]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEShaw194276–80-86) doubled enrollment,[[82]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEShaw194276–80-86) and increased the faculty.[[82]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEShaw194276–80-86) He secured more state aid and alumni support to fund the university's capital needs,[[82]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEShaw194276–80-86) including the gothic [Law Quadrangle](/wiki/University_of_Michigan_Law_School#Campus "University of Michigan Law School"), [Martha Cook Building](/wiki/Martha_Cook_Building "Martha Cook Building"), [Hill Auditorium](/wiki/Hill_Auditorium "Hill Auditorium"), and [Michigan Union](/wiki/Michigan_Union "Michigan Union"), which became campus landmarks.
